open_points.subject: A14 Required test 7
open_points.text:
and each such action, accepted, writes the audit action its row
   names (rule 1).
open_points.question: Must this say that the accepted action writes an entry only when it changes state, except that erasing old entries always writes one, so that accepted no-op actions remain covered by rules 1 and 3?
options: Qualify the requirement with changed state and the erasure-of-old-entries exception.
Require every accepted listed owner action to write an entry, including accepted no-ops.
open_points.default_guess: Qualify it to agree with A14 rules 1 and 3 and Required test 2.

witness.initial: A project is already archived and the owner has a valid session and submits archive again with the current revision.
events: The owner submits the archive action.
Registry accepts it as an unchanged repeat under A04 and A14 rule 3.
outcomes: A14 rule 3 and Required test 2 leave the audit log unchanged and mint no confirmation id.
A14 Required test 7 writes the audit action named by the OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS row because the action was accepted.
witness.observer: The owner reading the audit log sees whether a new entry exists.

open_points.subject: A21 review of A13 rule 6
open_points.text:
A13 rule 6 states what the digest of a
confirmation's inputs guarantees — one unambiguous encoding of the action,
target, version and inputs under a collision-resistant cryptographic
digest, a collision of that digest outside the guarantee — and test 12
shows that changing any of them is refused.
open_points.question: Does “changing any of them is refused” exclude a different encoding whose digest collides with the bound digest, as A13 rule 6 and test 12 do, or does A21 assert refusal even for that case?
options: State explicitly that test 12 shows refusal for every listed change except a digest collision.
Require refusal even when the changed tuple has the same digest, which would require retaining or comparing more than the digest.
open_points.default_guess: Make the collision exception explicit in A21 so it matches A13 rule 6 and Required test 12.

witness.initial: A session holds a valid pending confirmation for one tuple, and a different tuple has a different unambiguous encoding but the same digest.
events: The owner submits the different tuple with the pending confirmation value before expiry.
Registry performs the confirmation binding check.
outcomes: Under A13 rule 6, equality of the digests satisfies the binding check; collision behavior is outside the refusal guarantee.
Read literally, A21's statement that changing any component is refused requires refusal.
witness.observer: The owner sees whether the changed submission is accepted or refused.

open_points.subject: A13 confirmation digest algorithm
open_points.text: The digest is a collision-resistant cryptographic digest
open_points.question: Which concrete digest algorithm and output size will generated code use?
options: Use another reviewed collision-resistant digest supported by the selected runtime dependencies.
open_points.default_guess: Use SHA-256 through the runtime's standard cryptographic library.
consequences: SHA-256 is widely available and sufficient for ephemeral confirmation binding.
SHA-512/256 gives a different implementation dependency and performance profile while retaining a 256-bit result.
Another algorithm requires the factory to establish its availability and collision-resistance suitability.
open_points.requirement: The digest is a collision-resistant cryptographic digest of one unambiguous encoding of the action, the target, the version and the inputs in that order, every list in its order and an absent value told apart from an empty one, so that two different tuples never share an encoding; that two encodings share a digest is outside the guarantee.

open_points.subject: A13 confirmation tuple encoding
open_points.text: one unambiguous encoding of the action, the target, the version and the inputs in that order, every list in its order and an absent value told apart from an empty one
open_points.question: What exact encoding will generated code use to make value boundaries, types, list order, Unicode text and absent versus empty values unambiguous?
options: Canonical JSON with explicit type and absence tags and a fixed Unicode/byte convention.
A dedicated canonical encoder over the request models.
open_points.default_guess: Use a dedicated canonical encoder with explicit type tags, length prefixes and UTF-8 text, preserving list order.
consequences: Canonical JSON is inspectable but needs fully fixed rules for numbers, keys, Unicode and absence tags.
A typed binary encoding makes boundaries explicit but is less human-readable and needs its own encoder checks.
A model-specific encoder is narrow and simple but must be updated whenever a confirmed action's inputs change.
open_points.requirement: The digest is a collision-resistant cryptographic digest of one unambiguous encoding of the action, the target, the version and the inputs in that order, every list in its order and an absent value told apart from an empty one, so that two different tuples never share an encoding; that two encodings share a digest is outside the guarantee.

open_points.subject: OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS row values
open_points.text:
each such action, accepted, writes the audit action its row
   names (rule 1).
open_points.question: What exact audit-action member does each owner action, customer-mark transition and project-erasure kind name?
options: Declare distinct audit-action members for every M09 action and map each key to its corresponding member.
Reuse an audit-action member across transitions or erasure kinds where State 6 defines them as the same recorded change.
open_points.default_guess: Declare and map one explicit audit-action member for every distinct change M09 requires the log to distinguish.
consequences: Distinct members preserve the distinctions in M09 directly but enlarge the closed audit-action vocabulary.
Reused members reduce the vocabulary but are valid only if the resulting entry still records every distinction M09 requires.
open_points.requirement: Which audit action an accepted owner action writes — for a customer mark by its transition, for a project's erasure by its kind — is its row of the imported `OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS` constant (SPEC_STANDARD §15.3.1; State 1 M28).

open_points.subject: A14 Required test 7 witness binding
open_points.text:
7. The imported `OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS` constant has exactly one row for each
   owner action M09 lists, for each customer mark transition and each
   project erasure kind, the erasure of old entries among them, and no other
   row; and each such action, accepted, writes the audit action its row
   names (rule 1).
open_points.question: Which check will be bound as the witness that verifies the table's exact coverage and the behavior of every row?
options: Bind one generated exhaustive check that iterates the closed owner-action and variant vocabularies.
Bind separate checks for table coverage and for the runtime behavior of every mapped row.
open_points.default_guess: Use separate exhaustive coverage and behavior checks and bind both to this Required tests item.
consequences: One combined check gives a single witness but couples release-table validation to behavioral execution.
Separate checks isolate failures but the assembly must bind both checks to the one Required tests item.
open_points.requirement: each Required tests item has a witness check that asserts the invariants it names

open_points.subject: A13 digest and encoding verification
open_points.text:
a change whose encoding shares the bound digest aside, which
    rule 6 puts outside the guarantee and no test can produce.
open_points.question: How will factory verification establish use of the selected cryptographic digest and an unambiguous encoder without requiring a real digest collision?
options: Inspect that confirmation binding routes exclusively through approved digest and canonical-encoding symbols, plus property tests for encoding injectivity over generated values.
Use code inspection for the approved digest and boundary-focused tests for type, ordering and absent-versus-empty distinctions.
Use a replaceable test digest to exercise collision behavior while separately verifying that production wiring selects the approved digest.
open_points.default_guess: Verify exclusive routing through approved symbols and use property and boundary tests for the encoder; do not require a collision in the production digest.
consequences: Symbol routing plus property tests provides broad evidence but depends on the generator exposing a single controlled path.
Boundary tests are simpler but may miss an untested encoding ambiguity.
A replaceable test digest demonstrates collision behavior but adds test-only substitution that the factory must prove cannot alter production wiring.
open_points.requirement: The digest is a collision-resistant cryptographic digest of one unambiguous encoding of the action, the target, the version and the inputs in that order, every list in its order and an absent value told apart from an empty one, so that two different tuples never share an encoding; that two encodings share a digest is outside the guarantee.
